$comment: The grid of design/decisions/K14-the-grid.md as data, for the board. Edit the record and this file together.

goal.title: Everything falls out of the blueprint, for every building block in every output
goal.summary: Thirteen building blocks by nine outputs, 117 cards, each an eval with a stated green and stated evidence. Done is every card green or agreed not needed, then one story proves it whole: a fresh folder, the real ortho command, a new project, and the links app grown through its four stages.
body: **What Orthograph promises.** You write a blueprint: the things your app keeps, the operations that change them, the steps each operation takes, the machine each thing moves through, the events a move emits, the errors a call can be refused with, the roles allowed to call, which fields are private or secret, the environments and stores it runs in, the plugins it mounts, where an operation runs, and the journeys that prove it works. Everything else falls out of that one declaration for free: the model, the HTTP API, the server, the SDK, the CLI, the MCP tools, the docs, the portal and the telemetry. Nothing is configured twice, and nothing an output shows is written by hand.

**Why a grid measures it.** "Falls out for free" is a claim about every pair of building block and output. The coverage audit of 19 November (K12) drew that as a grid of 13 building blocks by 9 outputs, 117 cells, and found the claim fully true only for operations. A promise that holds for one row is not yet the promise. So the grid is the goal: each row is a lane, each cell in it is a card, and each card is an eval. A card says, in one or two sentences, what green means for that building block in that output, and names the evidence that proves it: an e2e check, a journey run through that output, or a view in the portal. A card is green only when its evidence runs in CI and passes. A card that exists in code but has no evidence is not green; it is "built, unproved", and the board shows it amber.

**What "done" looks like.** Every card is green, or Aaron has agreed it is not needed by design. A "not needed" card is not deleted: it stays on the board, greyed, with the one-line reason, so nobody reopens it by accident and anyone can see the grid is whole. Where an absence is itself a safety property (no secret field leaves through any output, no step leaks into a client's contract), the card stays live and its evidence proves the absence. When the last card turns green, the end-to-end story below runs from a fresh folder through all four stages of the links app, and the grid stays green after it.

**How it relates to the gates.** The grid does not replace the milestones; it is how we see them. Gate M1 (M1.15) is the first band: the basics of things, operations, steps, machines, events and errors in every output (K13's 5 by 5, M1.41 and M1.42), one visibility rule (M1.35), telemetry that carries the model (M1.36), and the portal as a viewer (M1.13). Gate M2, "workable" (M2.12, also the stage 1 gate), is the second: roles and principals (M2.01 to M2.07), secrets by declaration (M2.04), journeys run through the SDK, CLI and MCP (M2.08) so those three columns are proved by journeys rather than by hand-picked calls, `ortho new` (M2.09) so the story can start from nothing, and `ortho add` for the blocks that edit files in place (M2.14 to M2.16). The v1.0 stages fill the rest: stage 2 (ST2.06) the device lane and the adapter half of the mount lane, stage 3 (ST3.08) stores on a chain and workflows, stage 4 (ST4.08) the visibility lane at its hardest, a club whose members never show. The lanes this grid does not have yet (workflows, views, agents, chains as stores) join it as rows when their milestone's decision slice names their outputs; until then they are listed under "Rows still to come".

**How we use it.** The board shows one lane per row, its cards left to right in the column order below, each card green, amber (built, unproved), red (missing) or grey (not needed, agreed). Work is picked by lane, not by cell: a lane is climbed until it is fully green, so at each step we know exactly which building block is whole. The order is under "Hill-climb order".

states.green: the card's evidence runs in CI and passes
states.amber: built, but no evidence runs yet
states.grey: agreed not needed by design (Aaron, Q2); absence checks stay live

lanes.name: Operation & read
lanes.endState: Every operation and read is one endpoint, one SDK function, one CLI command, one MCP tool, one docs page and one portal page, with its description, who may call, its idempotency and its budget, and every call is counted and traced.
lanes.proof: The operation's page in the portal (the in-and-out band, the spine, the proof tab with its journeys' verdicts) and the operations matrix on home (calls, refused, defects, p95 against budget); journeys through each client (M2.08).

cards.greenMeans: Each operation and read is in the model with its kind, description, payload, answer, allowed, idempotency, budget, list options, `via` and `runs`.
cards.todayNote: OperationModel carries kind operation|read, name, description, payload, answer, allowed, budget, idempotent, list, via, runs.

cards.greenMeans: One endpoint per operation and read, its schemas from the declaration.
cards.todayNote: One HttpApiEndpoint per operation and per read (POST /thing/verb), payload/success schemas from the declaration, plus declaration re-exported.

cards.greenMeans: Each operation is served through its handler and each read generically, with the role check and a span.
cards.todayNote: Handlers.serve per operation, Reads.serve generically per read (role check, span, no handler); both wired in the server main.

cards.greenMeans: One function per operation and read, with the description as its doc comment, calling the API.
cards.evidence: e2e/m1/14-clients.test.ts; M1.41 calls every operation once through the SDK; M2.08 runs journeys `--through sdk`.
cards.todayNote: One function per operation including reads (examples/acme/generated/sdk/src/organization/get.ts), with the description as doc comment.

cards.greenMeans: One command per operation and read whose `--help` is the operation's description; a refusal exits with its declared code.
cards.evidence: e2e/m1/14-clients.test.ts; M1.41 calls every operation through the CLI; M2.08 runs journeys `--through cli`.
cards.todayNote: One command per operation and read, a flag per payload field. The operation's description is only a doc comment in the generated source, never the command's `--help`, so a person at the terminal can't read it. Regraded from the reader's ✓ against this card's green.

cards.greenMeans: One tool per operation and read, described from the model, reads marked read-only, operations closed to agents left out.
cards.todayNote: One tool per operation and read (allowance.get etc.) with description and the declaration's payload; narrowed by via.agent.

cards.greenMeans: One page per operation and read: description, who may call, read paging, idempotency, budget, payload, answer, refusals.
cards.todayNote: A page per operation and read: description, who may call, 'A read' line with list paging, idempotency, budget, payload, answer.

cards.greenMeans: Each operation has its page (the in-and-out band and the spine), and home's operations matrix counts its calls, refusals, defects and p95 against its budget; a read's list options, `runs` and `via` are decoded too.
cards.evidence: M1.13's screenshot of `handle.claim`'s page and the matrix lit by a journey's run.
cards.todayNote: Wire Operation has kind, description, payload, answer, allowed, idempotent, budget.p95Ms and detail.ts renders them. Missing from the wire: list (where/order/page), runs, via.

cards.greenMeans: Each call has the operation's span (`operation`, `attempt`, principal) and is counted in `ortho.calls` and `ortho.call.duration`, reads included.
cards.todayNote: Operation span named after the operation with operation, attempt, principal attrs; reads get the same span (read.ts:68); ortho.calls and ortho.call.duration per operation (call-metrics.ts:4).

lanes.name: Error & refusal code
lanes.endState: Every refusal a caller can get, declared or the runtime's own, has a name, a code and an exit, and the same three reach the SDK as a typed class, the CLI as `[code] Name` and its exit, MCP as an error with its code, the docs' refusals table, the portal's arrows and counts, and the span.
lanes.proof: Refusals on the arrow they guard and in the in-and-out band, counted by code (portal.md); M1.41's refused claim prints `HN-001`; `refusal.code` on the span (M1.36).

cards.greenMeans: Every declared error and wrong-state refusal has its fields, exit and code, and the model maps every refusal to its code.
cards.todayNote: Declared errors carry fields, exit and code; machine notFrom has error, exit, code; Model.refusals maps every refusal to its code (types.ts:190).

cards.greenMeans: Every refusal is a typed error with its code and exit, the runtime's own `InvalidPayload` included.
cards.evidence: e2e/m1/14-clients.test.ts; M1.41 reads every refusal's code.
cards.todayNote: Each declared refusal is a tagged error with its code, exit and the fields shown. The runtime's own `InvalidPayload` has no code in the model, so one refusal a caller can get has none. Regraded from the reader's ✓ (who noted the gap) against this card's green.

cards.greenMeans: Each refusal leaves the server typed with its code: declared ones from the handler, `NotAllowed` from the role check, the wrong-state one from the machine check.
cards.todayNote: Refusals are typed failures from the handler, NotAllowed from the role check, machine NotFrom, mapped to HTTP status by the wire class; InvalidPayload has no model code.

cards.greenMeans: Each refusal is a typed class in the call's error channel, with its code.
cards.todayNote: SDK re-exports Errors; each refusal is a typed class in the effect error channel with its code field and static code.

cards.greenMeans: A refusal prints `[code] Name { public fields }` and exits with its declared code.
cards.evidence: e2e/m1/14-clients.test.ts; M1.41's refused claim prints its code.
cards.todayNote: Refusal prints '[AL-002] Name { public fields }' to stderr and exits with the declared exit code; private fields are left out.

cards.greenMeans: A refusal is an error result carrying its code and name, its fields cut to what the agent may see.
cards.todayNote: A refusal is an isError tool result '[AL-001] Name { field: value }' with the model's code, fields cut by role; a defect is '[AR-500] InternalError'. The code is in text, not a structured field.

cards.greenMeans: Each operation's page has a refusals table: name, exit, code and when.
cards.todayNote: Each operation page has a refusals table: refusal, exit, code, when (declared, machine NotFrom, NotAllowed).

cards.greenMeans: Errors are decoded with their codes and exits and shown on the thing's page, on the arrow they guard and in the band, counted by code.
cards.evidence: M1.41 reads errors with codes in the data file; M1.13's screenshot.
cards.todayNote: Wire Operation errors and refusals are name arrays; no codes or exits in the structured model, and detail.ts:43 lists names only. Codes appear only inside the embedded docs markdown the page also renders.

cards.greenMeans: The span carries `refusal` and `refusal.code`, and `ortho.calls` counts by code.
cards.todayNote: Operation span gets refusal: <name> (and refusal.log) but no refusal.code; reads do the same (read.ts:67). The ortho.calls counter carries the refusal name only.

lanes.name: Thing & fields
lanes.endState: Every thing the blueprint declares, with every field's type, reference, optionality, visibility and description, is the same in every output: typed in the SDK, a typed and described flag in the CLI, an input and output schema in MCP, a reference page in the docs, and a card and page in the portal.
lanes.proof: The portal's home (one card per thing, grouped by `from`) and each thing's page, with the in-and-out band showing every field and its visibility; M1.41 reads every output for each thing's type and fields; the stage 1 journeys run through the SDK, CLI and MCP (M2.08).

cards.greenMeans: Each thing is in the model with its description and every field's type, named value, reference, optionality, visibility and description.
cards.evidence: M1.41 reads `generated/model/model.json` for every field's description; the compiler's model tests.
cards.todayNote: Things, fields, types, references, optionality and visibility are all in the model. No field has a description: `FieldModel` has no such key, and the blueprint has nowhere to write one (`Blueprint.thing` takes a description for the thing only, `packages/orthograph/src/modules/things/types.ts:27`). M1.41 asks for each field's description in every output, so M1.42 must add one to the blueprint and the model first.
cards.owner: M1.42 (it needs a way to declare a field's description first: see note)

cards.greenMeans: Every endpoint's payload and answer schemas are the declaration's own fields, so each field is typed on the wire.
cards.todayNote: Each endpoint uses the declaration's own payloadSchema and answerSchema, so every field is typed on the wire.

cards.greenMeans: The server decodes every payload and answer against the declaration's fields and refuses a bad one.
cards.todayNote: Handler decodes the declaration's payload and answer; fields flow through unchanged.

cards.greenMeans: The SDK exports a type for each thing (and its fields), not only one function per operation, so a caller can name a `Link` or a `Profile`.
cards.evidence: M1.41: the generated SDK exports each thing's type; ST1.02's journeys through the SDK (M2.08).
cards.todayNote: Operation functions take PayloadOf<typeof declaration> and return the answer, so fields are typed per call; but index.ts exports no type for a thing or its fields, only one function per operation.

cards.greenMeans: Each payload field is a flag typed from its value (number, enum, id), whose help is the field's description; an answer prints by field, not as one blob.
cards.evidence: M1.41: `links link add --help` shows each field's description; a mistyped flag is refused before the call.
cards.todayNote: One Flag.String per payload field, decoded by the declaration; flags have no help text (and the model has no field description to draw on); a single-field answer prints its bare value, otherwise whole JSON (cli.ts:77-78).

cards.greenMeans: Each tool's input schema describes every public field, and it offers an output schema from the answer, so an agent knows the shape it gets back.
cards.evidence: M1.41 for described inputs; M1.37's check (an MCP client lists output schemas) for the output schema.
cards.todayNote: Catalog entry has only the operation description and declaration; input schema is made at runtime from the payload (mcp/internal/tool.ts:86); no output schema is offered.
cards.owner: M1.42 (inputs described); M1.37 (output schema, in M3 since K13)

cards.greenMeans: Each thing has a reference page with a field table: type, reference or named value, optional, visibility and description.
cards.evidence: packages/generators/src/modules/render/render.test.ts; M1.41 reads the docs for each field.
cards.todayNote: Thing and operation pages have a field table with type, reference or named value, optional and visibility. No field has a description to show, because the model has none. Regraded from the reader's ✓ against this card's green.

cards.greenMeans: Home shows one card per thing, and the thing's page shows every field with its type, visibility and description, decoded from the data file (not only the embedded docs).
cards.evidence: M1.13's screenshot of links' home and `profile`'s page at a fixed `now`; M1.41 reads the data file.
cards.todayNote: Wire Field decodes only value/named/ref/optional; visibility is in the data file (model embedded) but dropped on decode; no description.

cards.greenMeans: A thing's public, non-text fields (and text fields marked `traced`) appear as `payload.*` and `answer.*` attributes on the operation's span; nothing else does.
cards.evidence: packages/language-effect/src/modules/handler/internal/attributes.test.ts; M1.19's "leaks nothing" eval; e2e/m1/16-visibility.test.ts for the telemetry audience.
cards.todayNote: Payload and answer fields become `payload.<f>` and `answer.<f>` attributes when public and non-text, or marked traced (O2, M1.19). That limit is the rule, not a gap, so the card is green by its own definition; the reader graded it ~ against "every field".
cards.owner: M1.19 (done); M1.35 moves it onto the one rule

lanes.name: Step
lanes.endState: Every declared step (its kind, the stores it writes, whether it is optional, and the adapter it calls) is in the model, run in order by the server, documented, drawn on the operation's spine and traced as its own span, and never part of a client's contract.
lanes.proof: The operation's spine in the portal: each declared step in its place, a finished call's spans down it, a running call's step signals as they arrive (M1.21); `ortho prove --empty` shows one red step per blank.

cards.greenMeans: Each step's name, kind, writes, optional and call are in the model.
cards.todayNote: StepModel carries name, type, writes, optional and the call (mount, call, mode).

cards.greenMeans: The endpoint carries the declared steps with the declaration the handler is built from.
cards.todayNote: Endpoint file exports a steps tuple of names; the full step declarations (type, writes, optional, call) ride along in the re-exported declaration the endpoint is built from.

cards.greenMeans: The handler is given one wrapper per declared step, run in a span; a call step goes through the adapter's runner.
cards.todayNote: Handlers.serve builds one wrapper per step: a call step through Calls.runner with wiring, others in a span with step.kind; the handler is given them.

cards.greenMeans: Steps never appear in the SDK's surface: a caller sees the answer or a refusal, never the steps.
cards.evidence: new: a generated check that the SDK's exported types name no step (Q1).
cards.todayNote: SDK function takes payload and returns answer; steps are not mentioned.
cards.notNeededProposal: Not needed by design: steps are the handler's inside, and exposing them would make every handler refactor a breaking change for callers (K13). Proposed as a live absence check, Q1.

cards.greenMeans: Steps never appear in the CLI's commands or output.
cards.todayNote: CLI command maps flags to the SDK call; no step shown.
cards.notNeededProposal: Not needed by design, as for the SDK (Q1).

cards.greenMeans: Steps never appear in a tool's schema; an agent calls the tool.
cards.todayNote: Catalog entry has description and declaration only; steps not in the tool.
cards.notNeededProposal: Not needed by design, as for the SDK (Q1).

cards.greenMeans: The operation's page lists each step with its kind, the stores it writes, whether it is optional and the adapter call it makes.
cards.evidence: render.test.ts extended; M1.41 reads the docs for step details.
cards.todayNote: Operation page has a Steps section listing name and type per step. Missing: optional, the stores a step writes, and the adapter call of a call step.
cards.owner: M1.42 (proposed: name the docs in its row beside the portal)

cards.greenMeans: The spine draws each declared step with its kind, writes, optional and call, and lights each from its span or step signal.
cards.evidence: M1.41 reads step details in the data file; M1.13's screenshot of the spine with a call down it; e2e/m1/13-live-steps.test.ts.
cards.todayNote: Wire step is only { name, type } and detail.ts:44 prints that; optional, writes and call are dropped. Live view joins step signals by span id (live/internal/join.ts) separately.

cards.greenMeans: Each step is a span named `<op>.<step>` with `step.kind`, and sends a signal as it starts and ends.
cards.todayNote: Span per step named op.step with step.kind (call, database, wait, commit) and start/end step signals as log records inside the step span (signal.ts:14).

lanes.name: Machine, states, move
lanes.endState: A thing's lifecycle (its states, its moves, what each move emits and the refusal for a wrong state) is typed in every client, documented, drawn as the lifecycle strip in the portal, and every move is traced from and to.
lanes.proof: The lifecycle strip on a thing's card and page, with move counts on each arrow and refusals on the arrow they guard (portal.md, "A thing's page"), lit by `move.name`, `move.from` and `move.to`.

cards.greenMeans: Each thing's machine (states, moves with from, to and emits, the wrong-state refusal) and each operation's move are in the model.
cards.todayNote: Thing carries machine {states, moves{from,to,emits}, notFrom}; operation carries move.

cards.greenMeans: Each move-guarded endpoint declares the wrong-state refusal, and a thing's `state` is typed as the union of its states, not a string.
cards.evidence: M1.41 reads the generated API for each machine's states.
cards.todayNote: The wrong-state refusal is declared on each guarded endpoint, carrying `state`. States are plain strings: no union type, so the SDK, CLI and MCP can't carry one either. Regraded from the reader's ✓ against this card's green.
cards.owner: M1.42 (proposed addition: `state` as a literal union in the answer schema)

cards.greenMeans: A wrong-state call is refused before the handler; a move sets the state and commits it with its journal entry.
cards.todayNote: checkFrom refuses a wrong from-state, applyMove sets state in the unit and commits it with the journal entry; reads return `state` (read.ts:21).

cards.greenMeans: A thing's state is a typed union in the SDK, and the wrong-state refusal is a typed class.
cards.evidence: M1.41 reads the SDK's types; ST1.02 through the SDK (M2.08).
cards.todayNote: SDK is a thin wrapper over the API client; no state union type, no allowed-moves listing. State is visible only as a string in a get answer and the refusal class's `state`.

cards.greenMeans: A `get` prints the state, and a command's help says which states it moves from and to.
cards.todayNote: No state types and no way to see allowed moves; `get --json` prints the state string with the answer, and a refusal prints `state`.

cards.greenMeans: A tool's description says which states it moves from and to, and its output schema types the state.
cards.todayNote: Reads keep `state` in list items and the machine refusal exposes `state` as public, but tool schemas carry no state enum and nothing lists allowed moves.

cards.greenMeans: The thing's page lists its states, the wrong-state refusal and a move table; each operation's page has its move.
cards.todayNote: Thing page lists States, the notFrom refusal and exit, and a move/from/to/emits table; each operation page has a Move section.

cards.greenMeans: The lifecycle strip is drawn from the machine on the thing's card and page, with live move counts on each arrow.
cards.evidence: M1.13's screenshot of `handle`'s lifecycle lit by a journey's claim.
cards.todayNote: The thing's page draws its states and a move, from, to and emits table from the wire. There is no lifecycle strip and no live count on a move, because no trace source reaches the portal yet (`packages/portal/src/modules/wire/service.ts:8`). Regraded from the reader's ✓ against this card's green.

cards.greenMeans: Every move writes `move.name`, `move.from` and `move.to` on the operation's span.
cards.todayNote: Writes move.name and move.to on the operation span; move.from is not written, and the machine's refusal writes no state. Subject state at call time is not on any span.

lanes.name: Event
lanes.endState: Every event a move emits is typed in the SDK, documented with its fields, shown on the thing's page with its fields, named on the commit span, and its committed occurrences show in the portal with the commit that wrote them.
lanes.proof: The thing's page lists its events with their fields; an operation's spine shows the event its commit emitted and the `on:` handlers it set off (M1.21's committed events from the journal).

cards.greenMeans: Each thing's events with their fields, and the event each move emits, are in the model.
cards.todayNote: Each thing's events with their fields are in the model; moves name the event they emit (describe.ts:80).

cards.greenMeans: The generated API exports each event, named, with its schema.
cards.todayNote: generated/api/src/events.ts exports each event and names it (EventNames.name) plus a names list; event schemas are per-thing events.ts. No endpoint or payload carries them.

cards.greenMeans: A move's event is written to the journal in the same commit, without its secret or private fields.
cards.todayNote: applyMove builds the journal entry (event name, public fields only, trace id) and it commits atomically with the move; the journal module reads entries back (journal/types.ts:16).

cards.greenMeans: The SDK exports each event's type, so a caller can name what a move emitted.
cards.evidence: M1.41 reads the SDK's exports for `Events`.
cards.todayNote: SDK exports operations and errors only; the API's Events namespace is not re-exported and no event types reach clients.

cards.greenMeans: Decided by Q3.
cards.todayNote: No command or output names an event.
cards.notNeededProposal: Proposed not needed: a CLI of operations has nothing to do with an event until events can be followed (M5.05). Q3.

cards.greenMeans: Decided by Q3.
cards.todayNote: No tool, resource or description mentions events or the journal.
cards.notNeededProposal: Proposed: events as MCP resources come with M1.37's resources, not before. Q3.

cards.greenMeans: Each event is documented with its fields and visibility, on its thing's page.
cards.evidence: render.test.ts extended; M1.41 reads each event's fields in the docs.
cards.todayNote: Machine table and operation Move section name the emitted event, but the event's fields are not documented and events have no page.
cards.owner: M1.42 (proposed: name the docs in its row)

cards.greenMeans: The thing's page lists its events with their fields, decoded from the data file; committed events show on the operation's spine with their commit.
cards.evidence: M1.41 reads events with their fields in the data file; M1.13's screenshot.
cards.todayNote: Event is a string in move.emits and the Machine table; the Thing wire has no events field, so event fields are not decoded or drawn.

cards.greenMeans: The commit span `<op>.commit` carries `event.name`.
cards.evidence: e2e/m1/17-telemetry-model.test.ts (written ahead, red: today `event.name` lands on the operation's span, not the commit's).
cards.todayNote: event.name is annotated on the current span inside applyMove, which runs before the commit span opens (service.ts:83-88), so it lands on the operation span; check 17 wants it on `<op>.commit`. Event fields are not traced; a refusal writes none.

lanes.name: Field visibility (secret, private)
lanes.endState: One rule decides, per audience, what each field shows: a secret leaves only in the answer of the call that issued it, a private field only to the roles it names, and every output (HTTP answers and refusals, SDK, CLI, MCP, docs, portal, spans, journal, logs) calls the same rule and fails closed.
lanes.proof: Check 16 renders every output for every audience over a fixture with a public, a private and a secret field (M1.35); the portal's "no leak" check (M1.13); stage 4's club, whose portal shows nothing that names a member (ST4.07).

cards.greenMeans: Each field's visibility (public by default, private to roles, or secret) is in the model, on payloads, answers, events and errors alike.
cards.todayNote: visibilityModel emits 'secret' or {private:[thing.role]} on each field, payload/answer/events/errors alike; public is left out.

cards.greenMeans: The HTTP schemas a caller is served are cut by the one rule for that caller: a refusal never carries a field the caller may not see.
cards.todayNote: Answer and payload schemas are the declaration's whole schemas; visibility is used only to build the CLI 'shown' list of refusal fields (api.ts:21), nothing is cut from an HTTP body.

cards.greenMeans: The server redacts answers and refusals through the one rule before they leave.
cards.todayNote: Refusals are rebuilt with every field but _tag, secret and private included; answers go out whole. No visibility module exists in language-effect (modules list has none); only mcp/internal/shown.ts redacts.

cards.greenMeans: The SDK's types and decoded values are the caller's audience's, so a secret never arrives where it wasn't issued.
cards.todayNote: SDK decodes the whole answer and typed failure; visibility is not read.

cards.greenMeans: Answers and refusals print through the one rule; `Errors.shown` goes.
cards.todayNote: Refusal print shows only public fields (Errors.shown); an answer prints whole (cli.ts:77-78) and --json prints the whole text(a).

cards.greenMeans: The agent audience: public always, private to a role held, secret never, failing closed on an undeclared field.
cards.todayNote: seenBy/shownOf redact answers and refusals by held role, hiddenInputs drops non-public inputs, fails closed on undeclared fields.
cards.owner: built; M1.35 makes it the agent case of the one rule

cards.greenMeans: Every field table (payload, answer, event, error) marks each field's visibility.
cards.evidence: render.test.ts extended; M1.41 reads visibility in the docs.
cards.todayNote: Field tables mark '(secret)' or 'private to <roles>' on thing and operation pages; refusal fields in the errors table not checked, and no audience concept.

cards.greenMeans: The data file's visibility is decoded and drawn (the in-and-out band marks secret and private), and the trace drawer shows only what the telemetry audience may see.
cards.evidence: M1.41 reads visibility in the data file; M1.13's "no leak" check.
cards.todayNote: Wire Field has no visibility; the model is embedded in the data file but the schema drops the key, so pages cannot show it.

cards.greenMeans: Spans, the journal and logs carry only fields the telemetry audience may see: public, and text only when marked traced.
cards.todayNote: Spans use traceable (public and traced/non-text) per field (orthograph/visibility/service.ts:20); journal writes only public fields; refusal logs use public fields.

lanes.name: Journey & starting world

cards.greenMeans: Every operation declares `NotAllowed` with its code.
cards.todayNote: NotAllowed is a declared wire refusal with its code on every operation; the contract carries it. The role rule itself is not in the contract (it is the model's).

story.summary: One run in a fresh folder: npm create orthograph links, ortho generate and prove, every operation through the SDK, CLI and MCP, the portal lit by a claim, then handles and auth mounted, then stages 2 to 4.

steps.step: `npm create orthograph links` in an empty folder
steps.proves: the front door works with no checkout of this repository
steps.describedBy: M2.09 (`ortho new` scaffolds `links` at stage 1, identical to `examples/links`)

steps.proves: every output is written and every journey passes on workerd
steps.lanes: thing, operation, step, machine, event, error, roles, journey
steps.describedBy: M1.41 (the loop through the real `ortho` binary), M2.12
steps.gap: M1.41 copies `examples/links` into the folder; the story starts from `ortho new` instead, so the two meet only at M2.09

steps.step: the server runs; every operation is called once through the SDK, the CLI and MCP; a refused claim prints `HN-001` and exits 3
steps.proves: the surfaces tier, for every lane in stage 1
steps.lanes: the surfaces columns of every stage 1 lane
steps.gap: M1.41 calls no MCP tool; M2.08 brings it

steps.step: the portal opens on links' things; a claim lights `handle.claim` and its move, its event, its commit; the proof tab shows the journeys' verdicts
steps.lanes: docs, portal, telemetry of every stage 1 lane
steps.describedBy: M1.13 (the portal opens on links' things, a journey's run lights its operation and move)
steps.gap: the portal wire still says traces and journeys are "unavailable" (`packages/portal/src/modules/wire/service.ts:6-9`)

steps.step: `ortho add feature @orthograph/handles`, then auth (ST1.03, ST1.07); the grid stays green
steps.proves: mounting keeps the promise: a mounted plugin's blocks reach every output with their `from`
steps.gap: no check reads every output for a mounted block's `from`

steps.step: stage 2: `ortho add feature @orthograph/wallets`; create a wallet on the device; be paid by handle on Anvil; a reorg corrects it
steps.proves: device operations, adapters, chain events, environments with a chain
steps.lanes: device, mount (adapters), event (from the follower), environment
steps.gap: the device lane's CLI, MCP and portal cards have no slice (see that lane)

steps.step: stage 3: a Safe with the budgets plugin, hats, owners sign above a budget
steps.proves: stores on a chain, workflows, agents under their own hat
steps.lanes: store, roles (hats), and the rows still to come
steps.gap: workflows and agents are not rows yet

steps.step: stage 4: the same on Aztec; the portal shows the footprint and never a member
steps.describedBy: ST4.08 (`the portal shows nothing that names a member`, ST4.07)
steps.gap: none beyond the stage's own slices

story.missing: Nothing yet runs the stages in one folder from nothing, and nothing reads the grid at each step.
story.proposedSlice: The story check (e2e/story), after Gate M2, written by an author who is not the builder: steps 1 to 5 through the real ortho binary, writing one verdict per card to the logbook (kind grid, keyed by card id and revision); steps 6 to 8 appended as each stage gate lands.
